submissions.findingTextShort: An older systematic review found possible PMS symptom benefit, but most included trials were low quality.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review of nine randomized placebo-controlled vitamin-B6 trials involving 940 patients with premenstrual syndrome reported pooled symptom-improvement signals, but the authors judged most included trials low quality and explicitly limited confidence in the conclusion; this supports possible PMS benefit rather than unconditional Grade-A efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: Patients with premenstrual syndrome across nine randomized placebo-controlled trials
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B6 supplementation in historical PMS trials
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Historical efficacy-era dosing must not be copied into modern consumer advice without current neuropathy-safety reconciliation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2024 nutritional-intervention review reported positive B6 signals but substantial risk-of-bias limitations across the evidence base.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2024 systematic review of 31 randomized trials of nutritional interventions for psychological PMS symptoms reported consistently positive vitamin-B6 signals among included interventions, while only one included study overall was judged low risk of bias and the authors called for more rigorous research before conclusive recommendations.
submissions.populationContext: People with psychological PMS symptoms across a broader nutritional-intervention evidence base
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B6 as one nutritional intervention among multiple studied approaches
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Positive consistency does not erase trial-quality limitations or justify page-level high-confidence grading.

submissions.findingTextShort: An 80-mg/day B6 comparator pilot found improvement in both treatment groups but had no placebo arm isolating B6 efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind randomized treatment-controlled pilot allocated 78 participants and compared vitamin B6 at 80 mg per day with a broad-spectrum micronutrient intervention for three menstrual cycles; both groups improved, but the absence of a placebo arm prevents attributing the changes specifically to B6 beyond expectation, time, or nonspecific treatment effects.
submissions.populationContext: Participants with PMS-related symptoms in a small randomized comparator pilot
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B6 80 mg/day versus broad-spectrum micronutrients for three menstrual cycles
submissions.uncertaintyNote: No placebo arm; use as supportive comparator context rather than definitive standalone efficacy evidence.

submissions.findingTextShort: A short high-dose B6 trial found an anxiety signal in young adults, but it does not establish routine anxiolytic treatment.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind supplementation study in young adults found lower self-reported anxiety after one month of high-dose vitamin B6 together with a visual inhibitory-processing signal; the short duration, high exposure, and healthy-young-adult context make this hypothesis-generating rather than evidence for routine treatment of anxiety disorders.
submissions.populationContext: Young adults in a short double-blind supplementation study
submissions.usageContext: High-dose vitamin B6 for approximately one month
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Any efficacy interpretation must be reconciled with dose- and duration-dependent neuropathy risk.

submissions.findingTextShort: A systematic review supports peripheral-neuropathy risk with excessive vitamin-B6 exposure and does not support B6 as a neuropathy treatment.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2023 systematic review found elevated vitamin-B6 exposure associated with predominantly sensory axonal peripheral neuropathy and found inadequate evidence that B6 supplementation improves peripheral neuropathy; this supports an explicit dose-and-duration safety floor rather than treating B6 as harmless because it is a vitamin.
submissions.usageContext: Supplemental vitamin-B6 exposure and peripheral-neuropathy outcomes
submissions.safetyContext: Peripheral neuropathy risk is dose- and duration-sensitive and should constrain high-dose efficacy framing.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Chemical form, cumulative exposure, and individual susceptibility may modify risk.

submissions.findingTextShort: A review warns that prolonged pyridoxine intake above 50 mg/day may be harmful.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A clinical review concluded that prolonged pyridoxine intake above roughly 50 mg per day may be harmful and should be discouraged while evidence for routine B6 supplementation in peripheral nerve disorders is inadequate; this historical threshold is safety context, not a universal modern regulatory cutoff.
submissions.safetyContext: Use as a duration-dependent neuropathy warning alongside current authoritative upper-limit guidance.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Regulatory upper limits differ by jurisdiction and should retain source/date provenance rather than collapse to one universal safe-dose number.
